newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch arrest drug runners off Morroccan coast.
newsitem.headline: Dutch arrest drug runners off Morroccan coast.

text.p: The Dutch navy seized a ship carrying 15,000 kg (15 tonnes) of hashish off the coast of Morocco last week, acting with Dutch police after a tip off, a Royal Navy spokesman said on Tuesday.

Commander Silvain Benistant said seven Dutch police officers boarded the Rein B., a small cargo ship registered in the Caribbean island of Saint Vincent, on December 17 from the Dutch frigate Abraham van der Hulst.
"The three crew members of the Rein B. were arrested after a search by the police officers," said Benistant, adding two were Dutch nationals and the third was Lithuanian.
He said the vessel was boarded in international waters after permission from Saint Vincent authorities.
The ship, which Benistant said had been on course for Western Europe, is being towed by the warship to the Netherlands.

Benistant said the estimated street value of the hashish was around 60 million guilders ($34 million) but could not say where the drugs came from. The biggest Dutch hashish confiscation was 17,000 kilos in March 1995. ($1=1.744 Guilder)
